# Security verdict (corrected): #318 (F266) at db4e27d25972f0044234830613cdde8ae1d9066a

Result: PASS (unchanged). This supersedes 113b977a, whose ordering sentence was too strong, as pij-alert-tarantula pointed out. The finding stands: no path replays where main captured. Static review, CI 5/5, merge state CLEAN.

## Correction: the ordering
`refresh_live_tap` (crates/harnesses/src/interaction.rs) increments `tap_drains` under the gate mutex, releases the mutex, then awaits `drain_pane_tap`. My earlier claim that any race stores an older count, so the next tick captures, is false. An observer tick can read the already-incremented count, capture, and store that count before the drain consumes its bytes. Separately, the replay path reads `observed()` and releases the gate lock before it decides.

Example: bytes arrive after the capture, the drain consumes them, and the fresh read then fails at `list_panes`. The next tick sees an unchanged count and can replay the earlier verdict. That residual is bounded by the 30 s `CAPTURE_BACKSTOP`, exactly as on main for every drain (main had no count check at all). The failed fresh read also returns `Err`, so it authorises no injection itself.

## Why the verdict still holds
The new condition `tap_drains == gate_drains` is only ever added to the old replay condition, and `TapAttach::Attached` only clears `last`. For any interleaving, the set of ticks that replay under this head is a subset of the ticks that replay on main. The check is a brake (removing it replays more), not a policy. It narrows the N2 window and does not close it under every interleaving; whether it closes the reviewer's N2a ask is the reviewer's call.

## Unchanged from 113b977a
The tmux adapter changes only return values (no new launch, argument or quoting change), and there is no new credential or file access. Public hygiene is clean, with no lockfile or manifest change.
